task_signatures.pattern: Asymmetric contamination in one condition of RNA-seq experiment
task_signatures.correct_strategy: Identify contamination source and direction; choose a high LFC cutoff that captures only extreme contamination signals while preserving true biological differences in the moderate LFC range
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Using a low LFC cutoff that removes genuine biological signal, or applying the filter in the wrong direction

task_signatures.pattern: LFC cutoff selection for quality control filtering
task_signatures.correct_strategy: Reason about the expected LFC range of true signal vs contamination signal separately, then select a threshold that sits between them
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Applying a standard differential expression cutoff (e.g. LFC > 1) without considering whether it is appropriate for contamination removal

failure_modes: cutoff_too_lenient: removing genuine biological signal by using a threshold designed for DE analysis rather than contamination filtering
wrong_direction: filtering genes enriched in the clean condition instead of the contaminated condition
conflating_filtering_with_DE: treating this as a differential expression step rather than a QC step
ignoring_asymmetry: not explaining why contamination is present in one condition and not the other
key_principles: Contamination signals produce extreme LFC because the contaminant is present in one condition and absent in the other
True biological differences between conditions produce moderate LFC — the cutoff must be above this range
Always identify the contamination source and direction before selecting a threshold
The answer is a filtering criterion, not implementation code
